title: Real stone editorial serif
prompt: Use case: logo-brand. Asset type: photorealistic cutout of four freestanding carved stone capital letters for an Astir identity composition. Exact text, once only: STIR — precisely four letters S, T, I, R in this order, no other letters or symbols. The first two reference images supply the specific natural weathered warm ivory limestone/chalky rock of the embracing-family sculpture. Do not include that family, any people, any A, or any base. The four letters must look physically cut and sculpted from the same solid rock as that statue: continuous natural solid volumes, large quiet unbroken planes, irregular shallow pits, localized hand-chisel marks and worn edges. Real sculptural material and edge depth, not a flat texture pasted onto type. Natural subtle imperfections. No regular or repeating pattern, no tiled surface, no horizontal or vertical panel seams, no brick courses, no manufactured embossing, no excessive all-over noise. Neutral frontal product photography matching the source, soft upper-left light, front view with minimal perspective, coherent identical lighting across all four letters. Align all four letters on the same baseline and cap height. Separate each letter clearly with balanced relatively close optical spacing. Entire four-letter row centered in a wide horizontal 2:1 canvas with generous blank outer margins; no clipping at edges. Background is genuinely transparent alpha, including inside counters; isolated letters only. No ground or tabletop, no studio backdrop, no color field, no baked checkerboard, no cast shadow outside letters. No bone, skeleton, ivory tusk, drips, organic flesh, medieval fantasy ornament, ruins, gold, bevelled digital UI, mockup or caption. Typography direction for this image: elegant editorial capital serif, slightly condensed and visibly narrower than a wide display font, graceful medium stroke weight, crisp but hand-worn delicate bracketed serifs and restrained contrast. Inspired by contemporary premium New York editorial lettering, with an especially refined S curve, upright balanced T, narrow serifed I, and poised R with a clean diagonal leg. These are substantial real stone carvings, but slender enough to feel sophisticated and contemporary. Keep letter proportions harmonious; do not make them heavy, chunky, inflated, or extremely hairline. Material fidelity to the first two references takes priority over their original font shapes.
